# Integrated SSR compiler — v61 (bounded planning and seed data)

## Motivation

Earlier versions generated backend operations and frontend views separately, requiring the model to keep routes, response shapes, form state, and shared application assumptions consistent across requests. More local repairs did not reliably improve external functional results. In the v49 run, two model requests timed out after approximately 541 seconds each, before application implementation started. Missing usage reports do not establish that those requests were free.

V50 changes the generation boundary: generate a complete, server-rendered feature with its data access and user-visible behavior together. The compiler supplies a reusable runtime and performs verification after producing a buildable application. It does not contain task-specific website implementations or hidden evaluation tests.

The v50 platform run (85e384f6b853) exposed a different failure: all three model requests succeeded, but the compiler rejected both the complete draft and the split designs with `Duplicate navigation entry: ('/', 'Books')`. The run stopped before evaluation after 6m04s and 49,596 reported tokens. The complete model response from this run was not available locally; a controlled reproduction using the same public BookStack Lite specification and a fixed complete draft reproduces the exact error in the v50 compiler.

V51 separates executable contracts from advisory observations at model-output ingestion. It coalesces equivalent route and navigation declarations, treats repeated shared-link observations as redundant metadata, permits differently scoped/conditional page observations, and records unusable advisory observations without discarding the application. Genuine conflicts in executable routes and shared destinations, missing explicit global navigation and invalid schema still require resolution. When a full draft contains usable code but its executable metadata is invalid, one focused metadata reconciliation request is attempted before split generation; existing code is preserved. The compiler records the generated replies and normalization decisions in `.arc` for diagnosis. Previously the verifier treated all model-observed page link names as globally unique; now duplicate checks are scoped to the compiler-owned navigation, with actual public flow locators and count assertions checking feature interactions.

The v51 platform run (e17f1c967d16) confirmed that the split design could be accepted (79.0 seconds, three normalized observations). The preceding whole-app request and the following root-module request failed with `InternalServerError` after 180.2 and 25.5 seconds respectively. No deployable root was produced; the run stopped before evaluation with 14,236 reported tokens and two missing usage records. The logs establish provider-side request failures, but not the underlying provider cause or total billed usage.

V52 introduces one explicit, shared model-call recovery policy. The SDK still performs one physical request per invocation. The compiler classifies the sanitized provider error, retries only required work on transient failure, respects Retry-After, does not retry credentials/quota/permission failures, and limits extra provider requests to six across the compilation. A failed draft switches to compact split design rather than repeatedly resending the whole app. Required design and build repair can retry once; module generation can retry twice. Four consecutive provider failures open a circuit breaker. A deferred module gets at most one additional attempt from the same shared budget after other independent modules have had a chance to generate. Optional verification requests do not consume recovery retries. These are limits on extra provider attempts, not guarantees of total wall time or total token usage (normal, design-correction, and verification requests also consume resources).

The compiler keeps the accepted design and successful module replies, checkpoints owner state, continues to independent modules when possible, and later recovers deferred owners without regenerating completed ones. Partial delivery still requires a real generated root and a successful build; it explicitly reports missing requirements. It never invents handlers or reports an unavailable application as a success. An entirely unavailable provider may still prevent completion. Reports include `.arc/recovery-policy.json`, `.arc/module-checkpoints.json`, and sanitized status information in `.arc/model-usage.json`.

## V53: behavior-contract fidelity

The actual v52 platform run (82a6efbf9dbb) reached 60.78 points, 6/12 tests (50%), 50% features, 60,179 tokens, CNY 0.3406 and 6m31s. Its one complete draft and two verification requests succeeded without retries. Its internal report shows 12/12 primary public workflows and 6/6 supplemental workflows passed. The internal pass rate therefore did not predict the independent result; the private failures are not available and their causes are not established.

V53 retains the SSR and recovery architecture and strengthens the behavioral feedback loop rather than adding another generation stage:

- The primary public suite is still built independently of the implementation. Valid individual translations survive malformed siblings. Explicit source roles and allowed alternatives come from the same specification contract as generation; generation receives the preferred role and can use one native record-opening control.
- The existing coverage-audit request now receives a bounded snapshot of the actual generated implementation as evidence to discover concrete missing public assertions. Expected behavior still comes only from the public requirements; a proposed audit check must cite a real source clause and use normal browser interactions.
- Deterministically derive up to six additional user-input variants from the public evidence, preserving the original scenarios. Where a user-created name/title is explicitly isolated and observed later, substitute an alternate user-chosen value throughout its actions and assertions. Where free-form prose is expected to survive saving/reopening, exercise multiline input. Declared restricted formats are excluded. Cases with explicit isolation evidence reopen a private shared SQLite file across fresh application and browser lifetimes. Variants are reported separately; they are not official benchmark tests.
- The shared runtime selects multiline textboxes for otherwise unspecified prose fields, respects explicit input-type/single-line overrides, and supplies escaped prose and semantic record-entry helpers. The browser verifier observes document navigation and form writes as well as API requests, so checks are less likely to accept stale pages.

Controlled test using the **actual** v52 model reply from the archived run (no fresh model calls, identical generated business code, original 18 flows and six new variants frozen):

| Runtime | Original primary | Original supplemental | New variants | Combined |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v52 | 12/12 | 6/6 | 4/6 | 22/24 |
| v53 | 12/12 | 6/6 | 6/6 | 24/24 |

Both failures were real multiline metadata loss in previously generated single-line fields; the data entered into the UI differed from the reopened value. Changing the shared runtime alone removed both failures. This does not establish that the two cases were among the six platform failures, or that a fresh v53 generation will pass the platform suite. The controlled result measures general input/persistence fidelity and validates the new feedback loop.

## V54: canonical record identity and whole-plan recovery

The actual v53 platform run (93aa0098819c) reached 58.78 points, 6/12 tests (50%), 50% features, 108,211 platform tokens, CNY 0.4762 and 17m48s. The archive records a whole-draft HTTP 502, successful split generation with recovery, a coverage-audit timeout, and a root navigation repair. Its final internal suite passed 12 primary workflows and six input variants. The independently generated v52 and v53 applications use different generation paths but have the same platform pass count. Their private evaluation failures are not available; no causal attribution of these six failures can be established from the score alone.

V54 favors functional correctness over further cost reduction. The new routing seam centralizes public record identity (`record_contract.py` and `record_paths.ts`). For conventional integer-key resources, the compiler combines the validated schema, literal route prefix, and source evidence of a public user-visible name/title used for selection. It maps eligible paths to readable, stable-key-backed addresses. For example, a public record with label `Project Alpha` and ID 12 is accessible at a route segment `project-alpha--12`. The exact ID remains authoritative in the original domain handler; the runtime normalizes route parameters and generates consistent links, buttons, form actions, and post-save redirects. A renamed record's old address resolves to the new name without changing its ID. Colliding readable labels do not collide in storage or navigation. Nested parent/child addresses preserve each identity. The inference is restricted to explicitly public named records and conventional compatible key schemas; sensitive personal resource kinds, private records, API routes, and prescribed URL forms are not adapted. The compiler does not contain application-specific paths or hidden evaluation assumptions.

The optional independent behavior reviewer now runs in two smaller source partitions for larger selected workflow sets, sends compact step summaries and bounded implementation excerpts, and keeps useful audit checks if another partition fails. For compact apps with unresolved observed public failures after local repairs, one whole-plan revision can regenerate a coherent candidate including changed schema or route registry. It must build and strictly improve the identical frozen source-derived suite with no loss of previously passing checks, or the already accepted application is rebuilt/restored. This allows recovery from a bad initial design instead of attempting to patch under an incorrect fixed contract. No revision is requested when the public suite is already green.

Controlled replays used the **actual** archived v52 one-shot output and v53 split output, retaining all original business code and SQL. Both original frozen public suites (18/18 each) still pass on v54. The browser observed 23 named entity heading/address matches in the v52 app and 44 in the v53 app. A separate real browser check on the unchanged v53 code verified rename/reload, old-address resolution, distinct stable IDs for colliding slugs, and nested child identity. These are additional runtime guarantees, not the official benchmark's tests. The external impact of readable addresses and improved independent review is still unmeasured.

## Architecture

### V55: deterministic resource compiler and recoverable workflow translation

The actual v54 platform run (936baeff8c94) scored 58.99, passed 6/12 tests and 50% of features, used 87,570 reported tokens and CNY 0.4591 in 11m03s. Both primary verification requests hit the 12,000-token completion limit, so all 12 public scenarios were omitted and no browser self-check ran. The platform only exposes the aggregate result, not individual failing cases; the three consecutive 50% results cannot be attributed to a specific private test cause.

The correctness-first default (`--resource-first`) tries a new declarative compiler for compact, explicitly public CRUD-style requirements. The model returns only a typed description of resources, visible fields and labels, parent relationships, operations, destinations and requirement ownership. `resource_ir.py` validates the supported language and explicit public control roles, and compiles that description to SQLite DDL, route declarations and one declarative handler module. `resource_workflows.js` owns the common lifecycle: native accessible fields, selected-record lookup, a single persistent create/update, no-write cancel, separate delete confirmation, transactional SQLite foreign-key cascade and parent-scoped child collections. Name-based route handling from v54 remains available. Free-prose fields are normalized to multiline when no explicit source format constraint applies. The source must fit this restricted language; complex business behavior, authentication, mandatory seed data, special URL formats, and other unsupported tasks use the prior unrestricted compiler. The resource path accepts no model-generated SQL or custom handler logic. If behavior checks still fail, the existing guarded whole-plan revision can try an unrestricted candidate and retain it only on a strict measured gain.

Primary public scenario translation now uses batches of four rather than one 12-scenario response. A truncated response is split into smaller batches; successful independent batches stay accepted even if another fails. Requests are bounded and omissions remain visible. Independent implementation audit remains partitioned. This directly addresses the v54 no-verification failure without raising a single response's output cap or resending the same oversized input.

Controlled experiment on the public BookStack Lite source: freeze the actual v52 public flows and source-derived variants. Replay the actual archived v54 generated modules unchanged on the same runtime, and compile a test-only fixed declarative resource program independently from the public requirements. No live model calls:

| Candidate | Frozen primary | Supplemental | Input variants | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Actual archived v54 generated business code | 12/12 | 6/6 | 4/6 | 22/24 |
| v55 deterministic resource engine | 12/12 | 6/6 | 6/6 | 24/24 |

The v54 code had reintroduced explicit single-line Description controls and lost line breaks. The v55 resource compiler corrects the input kind at its declarative seam rather than asking for another generated handler patch. An independent public project/task fixture also exercised number and checkbox fields, parent/child lifecycle, cancel and confirmed deletion. Auth/session and provider-recovery fixtures continue to exercise unrestricted fallback. These are actual local browser and database checks using fixed inputs and the local in-memory HTTP test transport, not platform pass-rate predictions. The archived generated applications and the manually authored test resource descriptions are not included in the submission. The real v55 model-generated resource program and external pass rate still need a fresh platform run.

- Read the supplied requirements and extract public constraints, including feature ownership and explicitly stated UI evidence.
- For compact specifications, request one coherent application draft containing a route registry, SQLite schema, and integrated feature code. For large specifications or an unavailable/invalid draft, use a compact shared design and generate bounded groups of requirements, with each group owning its routes and behavior.
- Materialize the application on a shared Express/SQLite runtime. Render HTML on the server, use ordinary links and forms, persist mutations before redirecting (POST/Redirect/GET), and keep shared layout and session handling in the runtime. Small client-side helpers support browser interactions where needed. No separately generated React-to-API contract is necessary.
- Normalize equivalent model declarations; validate the executable registry, schema, generated code, application build and runtime. Only then request public behavior scenarios and an optional independent coverage audit. Replay those scenarios against the actual built application; repair the affected feature and keep the previous candidate when verification does not improve.
- Bound model calls by phase, disable implicit SDK retries, recover required work using the explicit shared budget, and record individual request outcomes and reported usage. Optional verification outages do not prevent an already-built application from being delivered. A partially generated split application reports its missing requirements explicitly if its remaining modules can build. A complete provider outage still prevents successful generation.

## V56: resource execution and verification share one contract

The actual v55 platform run (81012b008cae) scored 58.24, passed 6/12 tests and 50% of features, used 93,268 platform tokens, and cost CNY 0.5217 in 7m05s. The archived trace shows the resource model request succeeded, but all 20 initial public checks encountered the same inferred literal-page heading mismatch. The accepted quality revision replaced the entire resource program with unrestricted code. The final `application_plan.json` reports `generation_mode: draft`; consequently this run did not evaluate the deterministic resource engine itself. Individual platform failures remain unavailable, so these observations do not establish the cause of the six external failures.

V56 makes the declaration compiler the single owner of the resource program's executable static heading and the verifier's corresponding source-derived heading. A named, source-quoted explicit title can override an inferred navigation label; dynamic record identity and explicitly named collection regions remain independent. The compiler also retains named placeholders when the public resource requirements explicitly refer to the named controls as placeholders. Fields without such source evidence do not acquire conjectural placeholders.

Resource build and behavior failures first revisit the declarative description, not arbitrary application code. A candidate is compiled through the same deterministic seam, and behavior revisions must build and strictly improve the unchanged public workflow suite without losing an existing passing workflow. If that revision is insufficient, one bounded unrestricted candidate is available; its actual generation mode is reported truthfully and the prior candidate is restored when validation does not improve. A mandatory build repair cannot silently replace resource handlers while reporting resource mode.

Controlled local replay of the **actual unchanged v55 resource model reply**, with the actual public requirements and compiled production Express/SQLite application:

| Compiler | HTTP and persistence assertions | Missing assertions |
|---|---:|---|
| v55 | 12/14 | Static heading consistency and an explicitly requested placeholder |
| v56 | 14/14 | None |

These checks exercise real route responses, parent and child record creation, persistent multiline metadata/content, selected-record update and confirmed deletion. They are not the 20 browser workflows or the platform's tests. The archived v55 browser report already establishes the original 0/20 common failure; a fresh full browser replay on this Windows environment was blocked by browser availability/startup. No new live model requests were made. New compiler regression tests separately exercise canonical headings, explicit-title precedence, placeholder grounding and resource-first recovery with rollback or explicit fallback. The full old SDK-dependent unit suite could not be started in the current Python environment because `openai` was unavailable. The v56 platform pass rate is unmeasured; the best prior platform baseline remains v52 (60.78, 6/12 tests, CNY 0.3406).

## V57: native interaction and deployment-equivalent persistent verification

The actual v56 platform run (fb424b4487ac) reached 59.40 points, passed 6/12 tests and 50% of features, used 75,510 platform tokens, and cost CNY 0.4285 in 5m36s. Unlike v55, its final plan explicitly reports `generation_mode: resource`: all 12 primary public browser scenarios, two supplemental workflows, and six input variants passed without a whole-code revision. Consequently, continuing to optimize the same model prompts or repeatedly translating the same public scenarios has little evidence of increasing the official pass rate. The platform does not expose individual failures; it is not established that any specific execution condition caused the six failures.

V57 deepens the shared interaction runtime. A navigation button previously executed an inline JavaScript location assignment. If scripts were disabled, ordinary opening, cancellation and confirmation-entry operations were inoperable despite their native button role. Every `ctx.go`/button-mode `ctx.entry` now uses the standard HTML form-owner relationship: a visible native submit button references one independent GET form emitted outside the business form. This preserves the exact accessible name and button role, supports navigation inside an edited form without validation or submitting pending business fields, and preserves query parameters (including repeated names) and URL fragments. Save and confirmed deletion continue to use ordinary mutation forms. No task-specific routes, data or hidden evaluator assumptions are added.

The resource compiler's browser verifier now executes the source-derived public workflows in a no-document-script context, since declarative resource applications do not require generated browser behavior. Unrestricted candidates can still use their required JavaScript. Public scenarios that explicitly declare isolated business names and have disjoint observed name/title inputs share a persistent database across fresh browser/server lifetimes; cases with ambiguous or conflicting input identities keep separate storage. Supplemental variants have their own database population. The execution and storage profiles are included in the result report. This checks the meaningful application environment rather than adding more speculative model-generated assertions.

Controlled local comparison using the **same actual v56 model reply, real public inputs and compiled Express/SQLite runtime**, no new model calls:

| Execution condition | v56 | v57 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native HTTP/form-owner and data-isolation assertions | 7/17 | 17/17 |
| Actual 20 frozen public scenarios, replayed over native HTML/HTTP without evaluating document scripts | 5/20 | 20/20 |
| Previous ordinary HTTP/persistence regression assertions on v57 | — | 14/14 |

The frozen replay used the unchanged 12 primary, two supplemental, and six variant flows recorded in the actual v56 run. Eleven safely isolated primary cases shared one SQLite file, six variants shared a separate file, and three other cases each used an independent database. SQLite connections were closed and reopened per scenario. Native replay selected actual controls and form owners from rendered HTML, submitted the ordinary fields and followed redirects; it did not claim full browser visibility or layout equivalence. All five SDK-independent compiler regressions in the resource-contract and execution-profile suites passed. Full browser testing on the local Windows environment remains unavailable; the new browser profile in the platform run must be validated there. These measurements establish genuine native-interaction and persistent-data robustness, not an attribution or prediction of the external test results. If v57 still receives 50%, preserve v56 and evaluate the exact same compiler against a different supported public task rather than continuously specializing to this one aggregate score.

## V58: progressive interface planning and generation recovery

The v57 cross-task platform experiment changed the research direction. BookStack remained at 6/12 tests (50%), score 57.88, CNY 0.5550 and 7m12s. The 12306 railway-travel Lite run (89d0247cacf4) received 0% because compilation terminated **before evaluation**: two complete `design` requests both reached the model output limit after 83.8s and 80.2s, for 99,615 combined reported tokens and CNY 0.2692. This is evidence of a scalability failure in planning, not evidence that a deployed 12306 application failed its functional tests. The actual 12306 Lite source/output archive is not available locally.

V57 already split application implementations but still required one complete schema/routes/navigation plan in one model response. V58 separates global interface construction from detailed route planning. The compiler owns the shared SQL/route registry, deterministic requirement-owner partitions, and a reserved root owner; bounded foundation passes receive a compact whole-source catalog and reserve cross-owner entrances and shared data. Local planning passes see the exact owned source, dependency descriptions, accepted schema, route reservations, and source controls. They may extend the shared database with compatible related tables and source-required seeds but cannot silently redefine accepted tables or transfer route ownership. The resulting complete plan still passes the original canonical route, SQLite idempotence, and source-contract validation. No code is generated before the interface is coherent.

A truncated or invalid multi-owner batch is subdivided; even a single owner can be subdivided by requirement IDs while retaining the same owner and merging its accepted route fragments. Invalid singletons receive at most one focused metadata correction. An accepted fragment is not regenerated; rejected fragments are applied transactionally to a copy of the registry. Batch widths learn from size failures so later batches do not repeat an already oversized request. The accepted interface and coverage are checkpointed in `.arc/progressive-interface.json` and `.arc/progressive-planning.json`. This is in-run recovery and diagnostic checkpointing, not an automatic cross-run resume guarantee. Compact successful draft/resource paths retain their existing behavior; a compact split-design truncation switches strategy immediately. Terminal provider authorization/billing failures still stop under the existing bounded recovery policy.

The same approach applies to implementation: a truncated progressive module is divided into disjoint handler fragments. Each fragment receives the accepted shared route/data interface and full owning source; local JavaScript syntax is checked before linking. A deterministic wrapper isolates each fragment's private functions and checks the declared handler keys at normal startup. The public route/schema contract is not rewritten on a truncation. Generation fragments and accepted/rejected attempts are recorded under `.arc/model-module-*-shards.json`. Other module implementations receive a compact DDL-only shared schema description rather than unrelated seed values and repeated prerequisite scenarios; actual final SQL/seed data remains intact.

Validation used an independently written 93-leaf public workspace fixture with a deterministic simulated model provider that truncates large planning requests, rejects a route collision and truncates one entire module implementation. No actual 12306 reply or live model calls were available for the comparison:

| Stress test | v57 | v58 |
|---|---|---|
| Same capped-provider simulation | Design truncated twice; compilation exits | All 93 requirement IDs retained; 23 modules, 46 routes |
| Real TypeScript/Express/SQLite production build | Not reached | Completed |
| HTTP entry, submitted write, and cross-area persisted-data isolation | Not reached | 69/69 assertions |

The final fixture used 66 simulated model calls, versus 83 before adaptive batch-width learning was added, with identical functional fixture results. Additional regressions exercise intra-owner requirement subdivision, one-time compact-plan fallback, rejected interface rollback, and split handler linkage. All three new planning tests plus the five previous SDK-independent resource/execution-profile tests passed. Replaying the actual archived v56 BookStack resource reply through v58 also preserved the previous 17/17 native interaction/persistence assertions. These are genuine local compiler/runtime checks, not official benchmark scores or a claim that 12306 will pass 69 tests. The next useful experiment is the actual 12306 Lite run: verify planning completes, count deployable owners, and measure external pass rate and cost. The 50% BookStack plateau remains unresolved; the validated resource route is preserved rather than speculatively changed again.

## V59: cohesive ownership and transport-aware recovery

The v58 12306 Lite platform run (55535ddea3e6) progressed farther than v57: the first foundation batch of eight owners/13 requirements succeeded in 83.8s, and the second eight owners/15 requirements succeeded in 83.1s. The final one-owner/three-requirement batch encountered HTTP 502, 503, 503 and 502. V58 incorrectly treated the temporary provider failures as an output-size failure, subdivided the final batch, and retried within seconds until its four-consecutive-failure circuit opened. The run stopped before evaluation after 3m13s, with 38,567 reported tokens, four requests without usage, and CNY 0.1567 displayed cost. This is an observed provider availability failure, not another model output truncation and not a measured accuracy failure of generated code. V58 BookStack remained at 50% (score 59.39, 76,975 tokens, CNY 0.4295, 7m32s); its individual platform failures remain unavailable.

V59 separates response-size/semantic errors from transport availability. The shared model-call policy owns bounded recovery for HTTP 502/503/504 in required compilation phases; retries preserve the exact request and configured model/endpoint. It schedules 12, 24, 48 and at most 60 seconds for the observed four-error sequence. At the former circuit threshold, a single delayed half-open probe is permitted for this transient gateway class, subject to the same six extra-request allowance and a shared 180-second availability wait budget. Persistent gateway failure stops after the bounded probe; authentication, authorization, billing/quota denials and terminal provider errors are never bypassed. Retry-After is honored, optional behavioral verification/revision does not silently consume required-work gateway retries, and an ordinary received-but-truncated response resets transport-failure state. The progressive planner and handler-fragment generator now subdivide only actual output/validation errors, not upstream unavailability. The policy records the classification, waits, and recovery events.

V58 also exposed unnecessary owner fragmentation: 31 source requirements were assigned to 17 modules. V59 groups small adjacent source branches into bounded cohesive owners for large-source compilation. Immediate siblings stay together when possible, adequate groups close at a major topic boundary, and both six-leaf and 28,000 owned-source-character bounds apply (an oversized individual source requirement is indivisible). Ownership remains one-to-one; local planning and handler generation still subdivide actual output truncations. Small successful resource/draft paths and compact split-design behavior are preserved. Fewer owners reduce duplicated foundation/route/implementation calls without reducing the source requirement set; the actual model-generated route count remains a function of the application's real behavior.

Controlled regression exactly recreated the observed three foundation batch sizes (13, 15, 3 requirements over 17 original owners) and the four gateway errors with a virtual clock and deterministic simulated provider. V58 terminated before completing the plan; V59 accepted the same third batch after bounded recovery, with no subdivision or repeated accepted batches. A separate whole-compiler test used the same 31-requirement synthetic source to measure the new ownership partition and actual build:

| Same synthetic source | v58 healthy provider | v59 healthy provider | v59 four transient gateway errors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Preserved requirement IDs | 31/31 | 31/31 | 31/31 |
| Owners | 17 | 6 | 6 |
| Foundation requests | 3 | 1 | 1 |
| Total simulated requests (before optional verification) | 26 | 9 | 13 |
| Real Express/SQLite build + per-owner HTTP/persistence assertions | 51/51 | 18/18 | 18/18 |

The HTTP suite counts three checks per generated owner (entry, save and isolated persisted read), not 31 independently validated scenario semantics; thus the denominators differ after coalescing. The outage run used four extra requests and 144 seconds of virtual wait, not live paid calls or real wall time. Six SDK-independent availability tests passed, including a persistent 503, a terminal denial, optional verification and a rate-limit Retry-After. The three v58 progressive-planning and five previous resource/execution tests still pass. The prior actual-build 93-requirement capped-provider fixture remains 69/69 runtime checks, with all 23 owners; the archived v56 BookStack resource reply still passes 17/17 local native-interaction assertions. No real 12306 source/reply or individual platform failures were available for local replay. Actual 12306 Lite deployment and external pass rate remain to be measured; a persistent provider outage can still make generation impossible. This version primarily reduces the chance of failing before evaluation and preserves the best prior BookStack path.

## V60: runtime-owned initialization and SQL-fragment reconciliation

The v59 Lite result contains six passing tests overall (6/182, 3.3%). BookStack passed 6/12, but the 12306 run (7f8ba97d7fd2) stopped before evaluation after 19m10s and 320,828 reported tokens. Its planning requests repeatedly subdivided batches after `Database initialization is not idempotent`, eventually terminating on one requirement. Other tasks shown as `Not run` have no measured functional results. The rejected SQL reply is unavailable. A controlled reproduction of the same error demonstrates a generic compiler defect: inserting a unique seed with `INSERT OR IGNORE` into an AUTOINCREMENT table increments `sqlite_sequence` on an ignored conflict, and the previous full-dump comparison rejected that otherwise usable schema. Moreover, repeating successful seed scripts on every startup could recreate user-deleted seed records.

The new runtime owns the bootstrap lifecycle. The compiler validates a fresh database using one atomic SQLite transaction and retains foreign-key, reserved-storage, and transaction-boundary validation. The runtime executes the compiled DDL and required seeds only on initial creation and persists a bootstrap digest in a transaction protected by the database write lock. It preserves seed edits, deletions, user-created records and sequences across process restarts. On an existing database with no digest, or a changed digest, it adopts an equivalent structural schema without replaying seeds; incompatible schemas require an explicit migration and leave existing records untouched. The model receives the same one-time initialization contract for draft and split generation.

Progressive interface acceptance now distinguishes SQL-fragment errors from route or ownership errors. A focused SQL reconciliation request receives the invalid delta, the accepted schema, the original proposed module metadata and source evidence. The corrected delta is tested against the entire accepted interface before committing it. Successful route metadata and earlier accepted batches are reused. Persistent errors still follow the bounded subdivision/correction strategy. This applies to any task with database-backed behavior; the declarative resource path remains a general public-CRUD eligibility rule, and neither unrestricted planning nor the bootstrap contains application-name branches.

Local validation used fixed synthetic specifications with 31 and 93 requirements (6 and 23 module owners). The model fixture supplied ordinary CREATE/INSERT statements, seeds with an ignored AUTOINCREMENT conflict, and one deliberately invalid column. For each specification the compiler reconciled the single SQL delta while preserving routes, built Express/SQLite successfully, and passed respectively 24/24 and 75/75 HTTP and database assertions (each includes 6 bootstrap/restart/legacy checks). The archived v56 BookStack resource reply still passed 17/17 native HTTP and persistence checks. All 18 SDK-independent Python tests passed; the SDK-dependent test module could not load because OpenAI's Python package is absent in the local environment. These are fixed-input local checks, not fresh-model or official benchmark scores. In particular, the new initialization mechanism has not yet been evaluated on 12306's actual model output, and BookStack's external 50% ceiling remains unresolved.

## V61: decompose an indivisible requirement by output dimension

The v60 12306 Lite platform run (2026-11-21 20:39–20:50) spent 248,989 reported tokens and 10m53s for zero official tests passed. Its six owners covered 31 requirements. One foundation response hit the completion limit and was split into two successful requests. Six local planning responses then hit the completion limit, including the final request for the single requirement `REQ-2.2` in `feature-02`. The compiler stopped before any application implementation or evaluation. The log proves the actual failure is terminal output truncation; the rejected model content is unavailable, so the relative contributions of schema, seeds, route metadata and model reasoning are unmeasured. BookStack remained at 6/12 on v60.

V61 bounds progressive batches by requirement count as well as owner count (initially 16 for foundation and 6 for local planning). It learns smaller limits from actual truncations and applies them to pending siblings; the largest already successful batch prevents one exceptional requirement from forcing every unrelated requirement into a singleton. The normal local planning contract is shorter and declares required seed-data ownership separately from executable schema and routes. Foundation and local completion budgets rise from 9,000 to 12,000 for additional reasoning headroom.

When a single indivisible requirement still exceeds the output limit, the alternate path validates a route-layout response and asks independently for the SQLite schema and seed requirements against those exact routes. Each alternative request has a 16,000-token completion budget. SQL deltas retain the existing reconciliation and atomic validation. Explicitly requested seed data is planned after the final structural schema, with bounded pages of INSERT statements, exact source requirements, accepted bootstrap SQL, and an explicit completion flag. A truncated seed page reduces its requested row count and retries that page. Every accepted page is checked against the accumulated database and frozen schema; invalid or repeated pages require correction. The compiler tracks seed coverage and refuses to mark incomplete seed planning complete. The v60 one-time runtime initialization applies the final bootstrap transaction on first startup. No task-name-specific branches or benchmark-specific data were added.

Controlled regression uses the same compiler entry point with a synthetic 31-requirement, six-owner specification and a fixed model fixture. With the v60 planning logic, both a multi-requirement batch and the `feature-02` singleton failed at the exact terminal error pattern. V61 completes all 31 requirements, even when the combined singleton response and first seed page are deliberately truncated; both source-required records are generated in separate accepted pages. The generated Express/SQLite app passed 21/21 real HTTP and database assertions, including presence of both records on the actual page and no duplication on repeated initialization. The 93-requirement, 23-owner v60 SQL-reconciliation regression also built and passed 75/75 assertions. The archived v56 BookStack resource reply passed 17/17 local HTTP/persistence assertions. All 19 SDK-independent Python tests passed. These fixed-input experiments exercise real compilation and runtime, but do not establish the quality or cost of a fresh 12306 model response or the official benchmark pass rate. An unavailable provider or unresolved alternate plan can still cause compilation to fail. No fresh paid model calls were made.

## Running

Use the supplied platform model environment (`OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and applicable `MODEL` / `VISUAL_MODEL` settings). From the compiler directory:

```text
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py <requirements-directory> --output-dir <separate-output-directory>
```

The default `--mode auto` selects the generation strategy. `--no-resource-first` disables declarative generation; `--mode draft` and `--mode split` expose the unrestricted alternatives. `--no-verify-public-flows`, `--no-coverage-audit`, `--no-input-variants`, `--no-quality-revision`, `--no-named-record-paths`, and `--repair-rounds 0|1|2` control public verification and routing. The generated application retains the supplied frontend/backend structure, locked dependency setup, `deploy.sh`, and `PORT` convention. Diagnostic reports are written under the output's `.arc` directory.

## Local validation and limitations

The development fixture suite includes actual archived v54 generated code, public scenario workflows translated in the v52 run, and test-only fixed declarative programs/fixed replies. No new live model requests were used. Real Express and SQLite handlers, production frontend assets and a Chromium browser were exercised through a local in-memory HTTP transport because direct loopback access was restricted in the development environment.

- Actual v54 generated code: 22/24 on the frozen expanded public suite; v55 declarative program: 24/24. A deliberately single-line prose declaration in the resource fixture is normalized by the compiler.
- Independent public projects/task collection: numeric and checkbox fields, child ownership, create/edit/persistence and confirmed or cancelled deletion passed.
- Independent account fixture: registration, login, logout, session persistence and refresh behavior passed.
- Independent two-module fixture: simulated whole draft HTTP 500 and three root-generation HTTP 500s; the other module was retained, deferred root recovered, and database mutation/reload passed. The successful design was requested once.
- Compiler unit suite: 31 tests passed, including previous recovery/normalization and data-fidelity checks, public record binding, private/prescribed route exclusion, independent audit partition recovery, plan revision, resource compilation and fallback, field-kind normalization, and adaptive primary workflow translation.

Fixtures, model replies, credentials, and generated applications are excluded from the submission archive. These historical v55 results establish the functioning of a fixed resource program, not the quality of a fresh model-generated application or an ARC-Bench score. See the V56 section for the real v55 model reply, the subsequent local regression, and the remaining validation limitations.

3:RESOURCE_PLAN = """Design a declarative program for a PUBLIC record collection application.
4:The compiler generates all SQL, routes, navigation, HTML, and create/edit/delete behavior. Use
5:this ONLY if all public requirements fit one or more public named collections, optionally one
6:level of child records (CRUD, display, cancel, confirmation, persistence). If any required
7:authentication, preseeded records, non-CRUD operations, explicit specialized URL formats,
8:filters, calculations, search, commerce, formatting editor or other behavior cannot be
9:represented, return {"supported":false,"reason":"specific missing capability"}.
10:Otherwise return a compact JSON object:
11:{"supported":true,"title":"App title","home":{"heading":"Workspace heading","text":"intro","covers":["requirement IDs"]},
12:"resources":[{"key":"plural_table_name","parent":null,"display":"name","covers":["requirement IDs"],
13:"fields":[{"key":"name","label":"Name","kind":"text","required":true},
14:{"key":"description","label":"Description","kind":"textarea","required":false,"placeholder":"optional source placeholder"}],
15:"list":{"heading":"Collection heading","region":"exact region label","nav":"global link label","entry_role":"button"},
16:"create":{"label":"Open create control","heading":"Create form heading","save":"Save control","cancel":"Cancel control","role":"link","cancel_role":"button","destination":"detail"},
17:"edit":{"label":"Edit control","heading":"Edit form heading","save":"Save control","cancel":"Cancel control","role":"link","destination":"detail"},
18:"delete":{"label":"Delete control","heading":"Confirmation heading","confirm":"Confirm control","cancel":"Cancel control","role":"button","destination":"list"}}]}.
19:Field kinds: text, textarea (description/body/prose), number, checkbox. A text display field is required.
20:Keys are lowercase SQL identifiers; they become literal URL segments and table names. Child resources
21:declare parent using the earlier resource's key, omit list.nav, and list.region describes the collection
22:on the parent detail. Child create destination can be parent or detail; root destination detail or list.
23:Set optional create/edit/delete to null if not required. Preserve exact public labels and roles, choose
24:the primary source role when alternatives exist. Preserve explicitly specified placeholders as well as labels.
25:For a literal destination whose public heading differs from its entry label, optionally provide
26:entry_heading_overrides: [{"page":"/collection","name":"heading","source":"verbatim public heading clause"}].
27:Save always commits, cancel never commits. Child delete
28:returns parent, root delete returns list. Map every supplied required ID exactly once to home or a
29:resource covers; don't omit a requirement to fit this scheme. Do not add fake controls, code, SQL, test
30:data, fabricated preconditions, or task-specific special cases. Return only the JSON object."""

32:RESOURCE_PLAN_REVISION = """Revise the previous declarative resource program using only the supplied
33:public requirements and observed public workflow failures. Preserve working behavior and resource
34:ownership; fix the smallest coherent change in the program's metadata or operation declarations.
35:If the required behavior cannot be expressed with the resource schema, return supported:false
36:and explain the missing capability. Do not generate executable code or SQL.
37:Return a complete resource descriptor in the same format, not a partial patch.\n""" + RESOURCE_PLAN

39:RUNTIME = """Generate compact server-rendered application JavaScript, not mutually dependent React
40:and API code. The compiler supplies Express, SQLite, a common layout, semantic HTML helpers,
41:native form submission and optional browser enhancement. Use standard JS, no new packages,
42:file writes, or external network calls in generated handlers. Every required flow is ordinary
43:user-facing behavior for arbitrary valid data. Never branch on scenario names, test data or tests.
44:
45:Every module exports exactly `export function handlers(ctx) { return { handlerName(req,res) {...} }; }`.
46:Every declared handler key is present. `req.params`, `req.query`, `req.body` are Express values.
47:`ctx.db` is better-sqlite3. Use ctx.all(sql,...args), ctx.first(sql,...args), ctx.run(sql,...args)
48:or db.prepare with bound values; preserve record identity and relations. ctx.now() returns the
49:declared fixed source clock if present, otherwise current ISO UTC. Do not use wall-clock SQL defaults
50:or Date.now()/new Date() for time-dependent domain content when a source clock is fixed.
51:
52:Runtime helpers, all return HTML strings except page/redirect/data/session functions:
53:- ctx.h(value) escapes dynamic text/attributes; always escape user data rendered in HTML.
54:- ctx.page(req,res,title,content,{heading:true,status:200,navigation:true}) sends an HTML page,
55:  one visible h1 of title and compiler-owned shared navigation. Options optional. Use dynamic
56:  record title as the heading on detail pages. Do not duplicate shared nav or the page heading.
57:- ctx.link(label,path): native link. ctx.go(label,path): native button for navigation without write.
58:  Use ctx.go/ctx.entry rather than inline click handlers. In ctx.page these buttons own a separate
59:  GET form, so Cancel and record opening work without JavaScript or submitting the editing form.
60:  ctx.entry(label,path,'button'|'link') is one keyboard-accessible opening entry for an individual record.
61:  Honor explicitly declared preferred_role first, including parameterized business-name entries;
62:  if an alternative role is permitted either works, but prefer the explicitly named primary role.
63:  Ordinary navigation uses links; state actions use buttons. Never duplicate controls to satisfy roles.
64:- ctx.button(label,{type:'submit'|'button'|'reset',name,value,disabled,className}); options optional.
65:- ctx.form(action,contents,{method:'post'|'get',className}); native forms only, do not nest them.
66:- ctx.field(name,label,value,{type,placeholder,required,id,min,max,step,multiline}); named input + native label.
67:  Unconstrained prose labels default to a multiline textbox; use explicit type:'text' or multiline:false
68:  when the requirements prescribe single-line input. Use ctx.textarea for prose/long content and
69:  ctx.prose(value) to preserve escaped line breaks when displaying saved free-form content.
70:  ctx.textarea(name,label,value,{placeholder,required,id,rows}); ctx.hidden(name,value).
